subject: maths
title: Chapter 1 · Test 1
summary: Chapter 1 test 1: integers, fractions, decimals, rounding, percentages, wages, simple and compound interest.
body:
This is test 1 of 4 for Chapter 1: Reviewing number and financial mathematics. It covers integers, fractions and decimals, rounding and significant figures, percentages and GST, wages and salaries, simple interest and compound interest. Questions get harder as you go.

Allow about 25 minutes. Work with no notes. Use no calculator unless the question says you may. Read each question carefully, write your working on paper, then choose the best answer from A, B, C or D. Check money answers make sense before you choose.

questions.prompt: Point Q is marked on the number line. Work out Q × (−6).
questions.diagram_alt: A number line from −2 to 2 in steps of 0.5, with point Q at −0.5
questions.explanation: Q = −0.5, and (−0.5) × (−6) = 3 because same signs give a positive. −3 forgets the sign rule.

mistakes.A: Step 2: Q is negative and −6 is negative — same signs give a positive.
mistakes.C: Step 2: you added Q and −6. The question says multiply.
mistakes.D: Step 2: you worked out Q − (−6). The question says multiply.

questions.explanation: Keep two decimal places (8.03); the next digit is 6, so round up to 8.04. 8.03 truncates instead of rounding.
steps: Two decimal places: the rounding digit is the 3 in 8.03.
The next digit is 6 — 5 or more — so round up: 8.04.

mistakes.B: Step 2: the next digit is 6, which is 5 or more, so round up. You chopped the digits off.
mistakes.C: Step 1: that has one decimal place. Keep two digits after the point.
mistakes.D: Step 1: that has three decimal places. Keep two.

mistakes.B: Step 2: that is 70% of $45 — what is left after taking 30% off.
mistakes.C: Step 2: you divided 45 by 0.3. Multiply instead.

questions.prompt: Find the simple interest on $1200 at 4% p.a. for 5 years.
questions.explanation: I = 1200 × 0.04 × 5 = $240. $1440 includes the principal, which is the total amount, not the interest.

mistakes.A: Step 1: use r as a decimal: 4% = 0.04, not 4.
mistakes.B: Step 2: $48 is one year's interest. Multiply by 5 years.
mistakes.D: Step 2: $1440 is the total amount (P + I). The question asks for the interest.

questions.explanation: −2.5 × 4 = −10, then −10 − (−6) = −10 + 6 = −4. −16 forgets that subtracting a negative is adding.

mistakes.B: Step 2: subtracting −6 is adding 6, not subtracting 6.
mistakes.C: Step 1: −2.5 × 4 is negative (different signs), so it is −10, not 10.
mistakes.D: Step 1: multiply first. Don't work out 4 − (−6) before multiplying.

questions.explanation: The significant figures start at 6: 6, 0, then the next digit is 4, so it stays 0.060. Writing 0.06 loses the second significant figure.
steps: Start at the first non-zero digit: the significant figures are 6, 0, 4, 8.
Keep 6 and 0; the next digit is 4, so don't round up.
Write the zero to show 2 s.f.: 0.060.

mistakes.A: Step 3: 0.06 shows only 1 significant figure. Keep the zero after the 6 to show 2.
mistakes.B: Step 1: that is 3 significant figures. Keep only 6 and 0.
mistakes.D: Step 2: look only at the digit straight after the second significant figure: it is 4, so don't round up.

questions.prompt: Noah's salary is $91 000 per annum. What is his monthly pay, to the nearest cent?
steps: There are 12 months in a year.

mistakes.A: Step 1: dividing by 52 gives weekly pay. A year has 12 months.
mistakes.B: Step 1: dividing by 26 gives fortnightly pay. A year has 12 months.
mistakes.C: Step 2: check the size — about $90 000 ÷ 12 is about $7500. The decimal point has moved.

questions.prompt: Find the simple interest on $2500 at 3.2% p.a. for 18 months.

mistakes.A: Step 1: 18 months is not 18 years. Change it to years: 18 ÷ 12 = 1.5.
mistakes.C: Step 2: $80 is only one year's interest. The time is 1.5 years.
mistakes.D: Step 2: $2620 is the total amount. The question asks for the interest.

questions.prompt: $2000 is invested at 5% p.a. compounded annually. What is the balance after 2 years?
questions.explanation: Year 1: 2000 × 1.05 = $2100. Year 2: 2100 × 1.05 = $2205. $2200 misses the interest on the first year's interest.

mistakes.B: Step 2: that is simple interest. In year 2 the 5% is worked out on $2100, which gives $105.
mistakes.C: Step 1: that is the balance after just 1 year.
mistakes.D: Step 3: $205 is the interest. The question asks for the balance.

questions.prompt: A jacket costs $198 including 10% GST. How much of the price is GST?
questions.explanation: $198 is 110%, and GST is one-eleventh of it: 198 ÷ 11 = $18. $19.80 takes 10% of the wrong amount.
steps: $198 is 110% of the price before GST — 11 lots of 10%.
GST is one of those lots: 198 ÷ 11 = $18.

mistakes.A: Step 1: 10% of $198 is wrong — the GST is 10% of the price BEFORE GST. $198 is 110%.
mistakes.B: Step 2: $180 is the price before GST. The question asks for the GST.
mistakes.D: Step 1: $198 already includes GST. Don't add it again.

questions.prompt: Isla earns $26 per hour for the first 38 hours each week and time-and-a-half after that. This week she works 41 hours. What is her gross pay?
questions.explanation: Normal pay 38 × 26 = $988, overtime 3 × $39 = $117, total $1105. $1066 pays every hour at the normal rate.

mistakes.A: Step 3: the 3 hours after 38 are paid at time-and-a-half ($39), not $26.
mistakes.C: Step 2: time-and-a-half is 1.5 × 26 = $39, not double time ($52).
mistakes.D: Step 4: $117 is only the overtime pay. Add the normal pay for 38 hours.

questions.prompt: $3500 earns $367.50 simple interest in 3 years. What is the interest rate per annum?

mistakes.A: Step 2: $367.50 is for 3 years. Divide by P × t, not just P.
mistakes.B: Step 3: 0.035 as a percentage is 3.5%, not 35%.
mistakes.C: Step 3: 0.035 is a decimal. Multiply by 100 to make it a percentage.

mistakes.B: Step 1: (−0.4)² = (−0.4) × (−0.4) = +0.16. A negative squared is positive.
mistakes.C: Step 3: 1.2 ÷ 0.3 = 12 ÷ 3 = 4, not 0.4. Move both decimal points one place.
mistakes.D: Step 1: squaring means multiplying by itself (0.4 × 0.4), not multiplying by 2.

questions.prompt: $4000 is invested for 3 years. Option 1: 6% p.a. simple interest. Option 2: 5.8% p.a. compounded annually. Which gives more money, and by how much? (You may use a calculator.)

options.A: Option 1, because its rate is higher

questions.explanation: Option 1: 4000 + 4000 × 0.06 × 3 = $4720. Option 2: 4000 × 1.058³ = $4737.15. Option 2 is $17.15 more. Comparing the rates alone is not enough.

mistakes.A: Step 2: work out both amounts before deciding — compounding can beat a slightly higher simple rate.
mistakes.B: Step 3: $737.15 is Option 2's interest. Subtract Option 1's amount ($4720) from Option 2's amount.
mistakes.D: Step 2: $8 is the difference in the FIRST year only. Compare the amounts after 3 years.

questions.prompt: A shop marks up its cost price by 40%, then adds 10% GST. A customer pays $231. What was the shop's cost price?
questions.explanation: Remove GST: 231 ÷ 1.1 = $210. Remove the mark-up: 210 ÷ 1.4 = $150. Check: 150 × 1.4 × 1.1 = 231. $154 wrongly adds the percentages.

mistakes.A: Step 1: you added 40% and 10% to make 50%. The changes happen one after another, so divide by 1.1 and then by 1.4.
mistakes.C: Step 1: $165 undoes only the mark-up. You must also remove the GST (divide by 1.1).
mistakes.D: Step 1: taking 40% off does not undo a 40% increase. Divide by the multipliers instead.
